focus: popularity pruning, structured line families, point-line concentration, and near-lossless sampling

messages.body_markdown: Yes. `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` now returns a whole-line restriction $G=G_0[T]$, retaining every core edge on each selected line. After extension and vertical cleanup, global $D$-peeling costs less than $2D/p$, so no arbitrary partial restriction $T'$ is used.
messages.subject: Whole-line core handoff

messages.body_markdown: Round 2 keeps exactly $D\le K_\theta d$. The weaker $D\le A_\theta d\epsilon^{-\theta/(1-\theta)}$ would leave $D/d$ unbounded and restore the heavy-factor versus cross-factor branch; bounded $D/d$ gives only $O_\theta(1)$ factor classes.
messages.subject: Bounded-weight interface retained

messages.body_markdown: `IE-L-FACTOR-LIFT` is isolated with the necessary non-strict bound $\Delta\le D<p$ and has no rejected evidence attached. Please audit the standalone formal-root argument through $C\sim Z-Q$; the subsequent cross-component aggregation is separated into `IE-R-FACTOR-AGGREGATE`.
messages.subject: Exact factor-lift audit

messages.body_markdown: Researcher-0008 strengthens the graph-only ceiling: an almost-regular full-support table has fractional half-cover weight $\Theta(p/\epsilon)$, and the exact two-line collision mass is controlled by the variance of accepted point degrees. Its audit verdict is `revise`, so these remain diagnostic nodes; both sharp examples already have the decoder $Q=0$.
messages.subject: Sharper graph-only diagnostics

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence graph
nodes.notes: All measures use uniform affine point-line incidence normalization; the scope is only prime $p$ and $100<d<p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and polynomials $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$ for all affine lines $L$. Define $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(L(t))\},\qquad \epsilon=\frac{|E_{\rm acc}|}{p^2(p+1)},$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg Q\le d}\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)].$$ For $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$ put $$e(G)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)},\quad \mu(G)=\frac{|X|}{p^2},\quad \tau(G)=\frac{|T|}{p(p+1)},\quad k(G)=\operatorname{mindeg}(G).$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching structured family
nodes.notes: The definition measures labeled constraint rank rather than the cardinality of the sampled family.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $d\le D$, let $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\},\qquad N_d(D)=\dim V_D,$$ and $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ For $G=(X,T,E)$ define $$N_G(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E\},$$ $$\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)=\{x\in N_G(L):\exists M\in R\setminus\{L\},\ x\in N_G(M)\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<N_d(D)$, and $|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>D$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Popularity pruning
nodes.notes: The formal conclusion retains constant mass; its proof actually gives a smaller deletion loss. The source audit verdict is `revise`, so the harness determines status.
nodes.statement_markdown: If an accepted carrier $G$ has $e(G)=\delta>0$ and $\tau(G)\le\sigma$, then, for $k_0=\lfloor\delta p/100\rfloor$, it contains $G_0$ with $$e(G_0)\ge\delta/4,\qquad k(G_0)\ge k_0,\qquad \delta/4\le\tau(G_0)\le\sigma.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component concentration
nodes.notes: This is the exact component-measure baseline for the cardinality sampler.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G$ be a connected accepted graph with minimum degree $k$, line measure $\tau$, and $C_*=2^{40}$. If $$k^2\ge C_*dp,\qquad k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\mu(G)\ge\frac{k}{4p},\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.$$

nodes.label: Component-sensitive reaching sample
nodes.notes: The sample loses only absolute constants but its size remains governed by line support.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `IE-L-COMP-MEASURE`, writing $t=|T|$, there exists $R\subseteq T$ such that $$\frac{4t}{k}\le |R|\le\frac{16t}{k}$$ and $$|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>\frac12\deg_G(L)$$ for every $L\in T$. Hence $|R|=\Theta(\tau p^2/k)$.

nodes.label: Component-sensitive decoder
nodes.notes: This compresses the accepted interpolation, extension, cleanup, and component recovery chain.
nodes.statement_markdown: If a connected accepted graph of minimum degree $k$ and line measure $\tau$ satisfies $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional square-root milestone
nodes.notes: The required small-line-measure component remains an antecedent, not a proved localization theorem.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $\Lambda\ge1$, and let $G_0$ be the popularity core with minimum degree $\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$. If some connected component of $G_0$ has line measure at most $\Lambda\epsilon$ and $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}\left(\frac dp\right)^{1/2},$$ then one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{\epsilon}{160000}.$$

nodes.label: Support-localization ceiling
nodes.notes: Thus the accepted cardinality/root-budget architecture cannot reach exponent $1-o(1)$ merely by finding smaller components.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $k\le C\epsilon p$, $\tau\ge k/(4p)$, and $k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2$, then $$\epsilon^2\ge\frac{C_*}{4C^2}\frac dp.$$

nodes.label: Universal-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: This obstructs graph-only sparsification, not soundness, because the same table has an immediate decoder.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$ there is a legal table with $$\frac1{2K}\le\epsilon\le\frac2K$$ such that every $R$ reaching half of every accepted line satisfies $$|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ while some constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Regular fractional-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: The source audit verdict is `revise`; this node is diagnostic and lies outside the goal ancestry.
nodes.statement_markdown: There is a legal full-line-support table with $\epsilon=d/p$, every line of accepted degree $d$, every point of accepted degree $d$ or $d+1$, and the global decoder $Q=0$. For weights $\lambda_M\ge0$, require for every line $L$ that $$\sum_{x\in N(L)}\min\left\{1,\sum_{\substack{M\ne L\\x\in N(M)}}\lambda_M\right\}\ge\frac d2.$$ The minimum total weight $W=\sum_M\lambda_M$ satisfies $$\frac{p(p+1)}{2(d+1)}\le W\le\frac{p(p+1)}{2(d-1)}=\Theta\left(\frac p\epsilon\right).$$

nodes.label: Exact two-line concentration identity
nodes.notes: This identifies degree variance as the only correction to the random two-line baseline; the source audit verdict is `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $a_x=|\{L:(x,L)\in E_{\rm acc}\}|$ and let $$\Gamma_2=\frac{1}{p^3(p+1)}\sum_x a_x(a_x-1).$$ Then $$\Gamma_2=\epsilon^2-\frac{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}p+\frac{\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)}.$$ In particular, $\Gamma_2\ge\epsilon^2/2$ when $\epsilon\ge2/p$, and equality in the variance-free formula is attained by accepting $k$ direction classes, where $\epsilon=k/(p+1)$ and $Q=0$.

nodes.label: Exact-linear endpoint
nodes.notes: The modal construction refutes this uniform endpoint but remains below every fixed $(d/p)^{1-\eta}$ trigger.
nodes.statement_markdown: The assertion that there exist absolute $C,c>0$ such that every legal instance satisfies $$\epsilon\ge C\frac dp\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c\epsilon$$ is false, already for $d=101$.

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal incidence obligation. The direct-decoder alternative is essential by both cover obstructions.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$ there exist $C_\theta\ge1$, $0<a_\theta\le1$, and $K_\theta\ge1$ such that, if $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\theta},$$ then either $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,$$ or there are a popularity core $G_0$, a line set $T\subseteq T(G_0)$, and $G=G_0[T]$ retaining every core edge incident with $T$, together with $R$ and $D$, such that $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d,$$ and $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Near-lossless parameter gate
nodes.notes: The constant $C_\theta$ may be enlarged without weakening the dichotomy; no characteristic-size hypothesis beyond $d<p$ is introduced.
nodes.statement_markdown: After enlarging $C_\theta$ so that $C_\theta\ge16K_\theta/a_\theta$, the structured branch satisfies $$\frac{D}{\epsilon p}\le\frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\le\frac{a_\theta}{16},\qquad D\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon p}{16}<p.$$ Indeed, with $\rho=d/p<1$, one has $\rho=\rho^{1-\theta}\rho^\theta\le\epsilon/C_\theta$.

nodes.label: Low-rank squarefree interpolation
nodes.notes: A kernel element is replaced by its squarefree radical. More than $D$ distinct sampled lines exclude a $Z$-independent radical.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the structured branch there exists a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,
\qquad A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0$$ for every $M\in R$.

nodes.label: Reached-root extension
nodes.notes: Only the accepted root-counting implication is imported; the rank-producing construction is supplied upstream.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every line vertex $L$ of $G$, the $D+1$ distinct reached accepted points force $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Primitive vertical separability
nodes.notes: The gate gives $\operatorname{wdeg}(B)<p<dp$, within the exact prime-field separability range.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content, $B$ is primitive in $Z$, $h=\deg H$, and $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}(B)$. Then $B$ is squarefree and $Z$-dependent, $$h+\delta\le D,$$ and $$\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$

nodes.label: Weighted ramification-line bound
nodes.notes: This is the accepted weighted-resultant estimate applied to $B$ and $B_Z$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If coprime weighted polynomials $U,V$ have weights at most $u,v$ and $Z$-degrees $r,s$, then they support at most $su+rv-drs$ common degree-$d$ graph lines. Consequently, if $r=\deg_ZB$, the number of graph lines satisfying both $$B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0,
\qquad B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$$ is at most $$(2r-1)\delta-dr^2\le\frac{\delta^2}{d}-\delta.$$

nodes.label: Prime-field vertical cleanup count
nodes.notes: This sharpens the round-1 generic $pD^2+D|T|$ count and avoids directional-derivative transfer.
nodes.statement_markdown: At most $$h+\frac{\delta^2}{d}-\delta\le\frac{D^2}{d}-D$$ lines are content-trivial or identically $B_Z$-ramified. On every other line, $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ and the nonzero polynomial $B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))$ has at most $\delta-d\le D-d$ roots. Hence deleting all nonsimple accepted incidences costs at most $$\frac{D^2/d-D}{p(p+1)}+\frac{D-d}{p}\le\left(\frac Dp\right)^2+ rac Dp.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless global cleanup
nodes.notes: Each edge removed by peeling is charged once to the vertex deleted at that stage.
nodes.statement_markdown:
After the vertical deletion, iteratively delete every point or line vertex of current degree at most $D$. Peeling costs less than $$\frac{D(|\mathbb F_p^2|+|\mathcal L_p|)}{p^2(p+1)}<\frac{2D}{p}.$$ The gate therefore leaves a nonempty graph $G_1$ satisfying $$e(G_1)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2}\epsilon,
\qquad k(G_1)>D,$$ with $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ on every line and $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$$ at every point vertex.

nodes.label: Simple-root factor partition
nodes.notes: Uniqueness at simple lifted points makes every star monochromatic, so factor selection preserves rather than averages vertex degrees.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Factor $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i$$ into distinct irreducibles and put $\Delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_i)$. Primitivity makes every $C_i$ depend on $Z$, so $$s\le\deg_ZB\le\frac Dd\le K_\theta.$$ The simple-root graph is a disjoint union of factor classes $F_i$, each preserving all degrees of its vertices. For some $i$, $$e(F_i)\ge\frac{e(G_1)}s\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon,
\qquad k(F_i)>D\ge\Delta_i,$$ and $$C_i(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0,
\qquad C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0$$ on its line and point vertices, respectively.

nodes.label: Factor linearization
nodes.notes: A fresh exact audit is required. Researcher-0003 P7 is audit-inexact, while researcher-0007 P6 is conditional and does not state this cross-component association.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible with $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}(C)\le D<p$. If a nonempty accepted factor class $F$ has $k(F)>D$, satisfies $C(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ on every line vertex, and has $C_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$ at every point vertex, then there exists $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$C\sim Z-Q.$$

nodes.label: Global factor aggregation
nodes.notes: Association to one fixed factor aggregates all disconnected factor components without Vinh mixing.
nodes.statement_markdown: For the factor class $F$ from `IE-L-FACTOR-CONCENTRATE`, $C\sim Z-Q$ implies $Q(x)=f(x)$ at every point vertex of $F$. Since every affine point lies on at most $p+1$ lines, $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{|X(F)|}{p^2}\ge e(F)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Close the direct and structured branches
nodes.notes: The direct branch is already terminal; the structured branch uses only a constant number of factors and loses no power of $d/p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: For arbitrary fixed $\eta>0$, set $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Since $0<d/p<1$ and $$(d/p)^{1-\eta}\ge(d/p)^{1-\theta},$$ the dichotomy and factor aggregation yield constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta(d/p)^{1-\eta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate line-versus-point soundness
nodes.notes: Blocked on the bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy and a fresh exact factor-lift audit. Work states do not assert proof verification.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, integer $100<d<p$, function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and degree-at-most-$d$ affine-line table, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

summary: Round 2 retains the exact component sampler and conditional square-root decoder as a baseline, while the integral, fractional, and collision diagnostics show why graph-only covering cannot reach the target. The main path isolates a label-aware rank-or-decode obligation producing a whole-line restriction of mass $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ and relation weight $D=O_\theta(d)$. The parameter gate makes $D/p=O_\theta(d/p)$ a small fraction of $\epsilon$; rank interpolation, reached-root extension, vertical $B_Z$ cleanup, and global $D$-peeling then preserve constant mass. Simple roots partition the survivor into at most $D/d=O_\theta(1)$ factor classes without degree loss. A fresh factor-linearization proof would identify one class with $Z-Q$ and aggregate all of its components into one global polynomial, avoiding sub-$p^{-1/2}$ incidence mixing. The two remaining proof obligations are the bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy and an exact standalone audit of factor linearization.
target_statement: Convert local line-versus-point agreement into a structured affine-plane incidence configuration with only a $(d/p)^{o(1)}$ loss.
title: Incidence concentration engine
